hooks.text: Deep beyond Neptune, a giant frozen world is stretched into an egg.
Why is a massive world past Neptune shaped like a giant egg?
A massive world beyond Neptune isn't round at all.

title: The Dwarf Planet Shaped Like an Egg
description: Deep in the Kuiper Belt, dwarf planet Haumea spins so fast that centrifugal force stretched it into an egg shape with its own ring system.

beats.text: Deep beyond Neptune, a giant frozen world is stretched into an egg.
beats.visual: Artist impression of dwarf planet Haumea showing egg shape in space

beats.text: In 2004, astronomers tracking the Kuiper Belt noticed a distant point of light flashing wildly.
beats.visual: Samuel Oschin Telescope at Palomar Observatory at night, 2004

beats.text: That rapidly flickering brightness revealed a dwarf planet completing a full rotation every 3.9 hours.
beats.visual: Astronomical light curve graph showing brightness variation over time

beats.text: Massive centrifugal force from the fastest spin in the solar system stretched its rocky body completely out of round.
beats.visual: Diagram comparing a triaxial ellipsoid shape with a standard sphere

beats.text: An ancient catastrophic collision likely kicked off this extreme rotation rate.
beats.visual: Artist impression of two large celestial bodies colliding in space

beats.text: In 2017, as the world passed before a distant star, starlight blinked twice unexpectedly.
beats.visual: Diagram of stellar occultation where an asteroid blocks background starlight

beats.text: That subtle shadow exposed a dark ring system approximately 70 kilometers wide encircling the object.
beats.visual: Artist impression of Haumea and its thin surrounding ring system

beats.text: Known as Haumea, this collision created the frozen world.
beats.visual: Wide view artist concept of dwarf planet Haumea with rings in deep space

better_than_last: Paces the mystery by establishing the extreme egg-shaped spin before revealing the unexpected 2017 ring system discovery, avoiding mid-script technical drag while applying the reviewer's specific beat 8 wording.
